# CRT-669 — Liquidation in chunks for CFDs

## Focus: Margin liquidation splits CFD-family positions by MAX_LIQUIDATION_QTY (Jira); OTC/DMA defaults from IPF; plain CFD and CFD_STOCK have no default chunking unless the field is set; opening/closing orders outside liquidation are not capped by this field.

### IPF — MAX_LIQUIDATION_QTY and defaults
- [CRT-1891] New IPF field MAX_LIQUIDATION_QTY is present for CFD, CFD_FOREX, and CFD_STOCK instrument types and accepts integer max order quantity during Liquidation.
> Default max liquidation qty = 200 for instruments with CORNER_SUBTYPE CFD_FOREX_OTC (per requirement text).
> Default max liquidation qty = 20 000 000 for instruments with CORNER_SUBTYPE CFD_FOREX_DMA (per requirement text).
- [CRT-1891] Plain CFD and CFD_STOCK: MAX_LIQUIDATION_QTY has no default (empty); positions are not liquidated in chunks by default when the value is unset.
> Align with Jira: CFD/CFD_STOCKS should not have default chunking.

### dxMC
- [CRT-1891] MAX_LIQUIDATION_QTY is visible and editable in the dxMC instrument maintenance flow for in-scope instrument types (create/update).

### Configuration change
- [CRT-1891] After changing MAX_LIQUIDATION_QTY on a CFD_FOREX instrument (OTC or DMA path), subsequent margin Liquidation uses the updated cap when splitting closing orders.

### Margin liquidation — chunking and concurrency
- [CRT-1785] When margin Liquidation closes a position whose quantity exceeds MAX_LIQUIDATION_QTY, the platform sends multiple market closing orders such that each child order quantity does not exceed the cap and the last order carries the residual; orders are sent simultaneously (not waiting for prior fills before sending the batch).
> Jira example: position qty 500 with max 200 yields two orders of 200 and one of 100 during Liquidation.
- [CRT-1785] When position quantity is less than or equal to MAX_LIQUIDATION_QTY, Liquidation does not split the close into multiple chunk orders solely due to this rule.
- [CRT-1785] When MAX_LIQUIDATION_QTY is not set for the instrument, the full position is closed with a single Liquidation order (no chunking by this mechanism).

### Opening and non-liquidation orders
- [CRT-1891] User can open or increase a position with quantity greater than MAX_LIQUIDATION_QTY (e.g. 500 when max = 200) without validation rejecting the order for that reason.
> Restriction applies only during Liquidation child orders, not to discretionary open/close outside that flow (per Jira scenario preamble).

### Completion and trading hours
- [CRT-1126] Margin Liquidation run that issued multiple chunk orders completes only when all Liquidation orders for that wave have reached their terminal states (e.g. filled), consistent with common Liquidation steps for started Liquidation.
- [CRT-1126] If Liquidation is triggered outside regular trading hours for an instrument, the system waits for market open before issuing the same chunk sequence (repeat Jira non-trading-hours variant).

### Rejections, retries, and IN REVIEW
- [CRT-1126] When one chunk order hits max external rejections per configuration while others fill, Liquidation ends with one order still rejected per the CRT-1126 rejection/retry path; portfolio Liquidation status moves to in review (per Jira reference to step 4 in CRT-1126).
> Capture STRATEGY/order identifiers for the Liquidation child orders for support and retest.

### WebBroker — visibility
- [CRT-1126] WebBroker Order book shows Liquidation-related orders and status progression consistent with margin Liquidation (including in-review when applicable).

### Adaptive — parity
- [CRT-1785] Adaptive: margin Liquidation for CFD_FOREX positions respects the same MAX_LIQUIDATION_QTY chunking rules as WebBroker when the feature is exposed on mobile (client_shell_impact default both); if Liquidation is not surfaced on Adaptive, document N/A with product confirmation.
> ! reason: Jira epic text does not specify Adaptive liquidation UI; confirm scope with BA if Adaptive must show chunk orders or only server-side parity.

### Out of epic (reference only)
- [CRT-1892] FX_SPOT Liquidation uses max tradable amount instead of MAX_LIQUIDATION_QTY — not the primary thread for this CFD-focused epic; track separately if regression testing touches FX_SPOT.
